newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes slightly firmer in low volumes.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes slightly firmer in low volumes.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed slightly firmer on Friday as Brent crude oil drifted higher but traders said the end-of-week action was very muted.

Nov gas oil closed 75 cents firmer at $224.50 a tonne. Dec Brent was trading at $23.96 a barrel at 1646 GMT, 21 cents up from Thursday's close. It had been trading at around the same level for most of the day.
"There is nothing new," one trader said. "A non-day and the volumes are pitiful. It is the end of the week."

Dealers had seen Brent rise in the morning, in what was widely interpreted as a small correction to Thursday's sell-off, to touch resistance at $24.05 a tonne. It then fell back gently and traded just below $24 for most of the day. Support was pegged at $23.65.
Intermonth spreads were little changed, although Nov/Dec gas oil widened by 75 cents.

Dealers said U.S. gasoline prices, which have been a key market indicator in recent days, had slipped into the background again after rumours on Thursday of U.S. refinery problems appeared to carry little weight.
Nov NYMEX gasoline was 0.32 cents a gallon off at 68.90.

Lagoven, affiliate of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela, was making arrangements to meet supply contracts for October and "a good part of November" to make up for lost output while the catalytic cracker at its 510,000 barrels per day Amuay refinery is repaired, a company spokesman said Friday.
This news had little effect on energy prices, traders said.
Lagoven announced on Wednesday that repairs of the cracker would take about three weeks.
